title: Togo protocol v1
description: Messages exchanged between the Togo app and the togo helper (`togo serve --stdio`). Transport: each message is a 4-byte big-endian unsigned length followed by that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON (one JSON-RPC 2.0 object, no batches). Max frame 1,048,576 bytes. `hello` must be the first call; every other call before a successful hello gets -32002 not_ready. Every response carries the id of the request it answers; clients must match responses to requests by id, not by order. Senders must follow the params schemas; the helper ignores unknown params fields.

Id.description: JSON-RPC request id. The app uses positive integers.

Request.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 call. Methods with no required params may omit `params`.

Notification.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 notification (no id). The helper ignores notifications it receives. It sends one kind, `event`, and only to a connection that called events.subscribe.

Response.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 response: exactly one of `result` or `error`. `id` echoes the request id, or is null when it could not be read (parse error).

Error.description: JSON-RPC error object. `message` is fixed per code: -32700 "parse error", -32600 "invalid request", -32601 "method not found", -32602 "invalid params" (with data {reason: human-readable detail}), -32603 "internal error" (no details, never secrets), -32001 "not_found" (no such session), -32002 "not_ready" (call before a successful hello), -32003 "invalid_path" (fs.listDir: path not absolute after ~ expansion, contains NUL, missing, not a directory, or not readable; fs.read and git.*: path not relative, escaping the session cwd by .. or a symlink, missing, or a ref that starts with - or does not resolve), -32004 "tmux_unavailable" (data {found: version string or null when tmux is missing, required: "3.2"}), -32005 "unsupported_version" (hello with a protocol the helper does not speak; data {supported: [1]}), -32006 "conflict" (approval no longer answerable; data {reason: "answered" | "prompt_gone" | "expired", by?: "desk" | "phone"}, by present when reason is answered; or a git write refused, data GitConflictData: nothing changed except for reasons partial and raced), -32007 "not_managed" (write call on an unmanaged session, including git.stage, git.unstage, git.discard and git.commit). `data` is omitted when a code defines none.

ManagedSessionId.description: Managed session id: `s_` + 10 chars of lowercase unpadded base32. Also the tmux session name on socket `togo`.

UnmanagedSessionId.description: Unmanaged session id: `u_` + lowercase hex of the tmux session name on the user's default socket.

SessionIdParam.description: Session id as sent in params. Any string is accepted on the wire; one matching neither ManagedSessionId nor UnmanagedSessionId gets -32602 invalid params with data.reason.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 timestamp. The helper emits UTC with a `Z` suffix and whole seconds.

Session.description: A tmux session. Managed sessions live on socket `togo`; unmanaged ones are read-only views of the user's default socket.

bib.description: Two-digit number 01-99, lowest free at creation. Null for unmanaged sessions.

name.description: Display name. Managed: Trimmed of leading and trailing Unicode whitespace, then 1-64 Unicode scalar values (Go runes, not bytes or grapheme clusters), with no control characters (Unicode Cc). Unmanaged: the tmux session name as is.

agent.description: Agent id from agents.list. Unmanaged sessions report `shell`.

cwd.description: Absolute working directory of the session's active pane.

status.description: `needs_you` while an approval for the session is pending, else the status the helper derived from hooks and output, else `exited` when the pane is dead and `idle` otherwise. Helpers without events.v1 report only `idle` and `exited`.

activity.description: Short description of what the agent is doing, or null when unknown.

muted.description: Pushes for this session are suppressed (session.setMute). False by default; always false for unmanaged sessions.

meta.description: Agent-reported model and usage, all null until an agent hook reports them.

HelloParams.description: hello. The helper answers -32005 unsupported_version unless protocol is 1.

HelloResult.description: Base helper capabilities: ["session.v1", "agents.v1", "fs.v1", "capture.v1"]; capture.v1 adds session.capture. A helper adds, only when the running process serves them: "events.v1" (events.subscribe, events.keepalive and the event notification), "approvals.v1" (approval.list, approval.answer), "mute.v1" (session.setMute), "push.v1" (push.pair, push.unpair), "git.v1" (git.status, git.diff, git.log, git.branches, fs.read, fs.listDir with ref), "gitwrite.v1" (git.stage, git.unstage, git.discard, git.commit and git.diff with commit; only alongside git.v1), "ports.v1" (ports.list), "upload.v1" (fs.upload). local.* methods are never advertised.

SessionListResult.description: session.list. Managed sessions first ordered by bib, then unmanaged ordered by name.

SessionCreateParams.description: session.create -> Session. agent defaults to "shell"; cwd defaults to the home directory and may start with ~; name defaults to the agent's display name; cols 0 or 20-500 (0 = 80); rows 0 or 5-300 (0 = 24). Unknown or not installed agent, bad name, or out-of-range size: -32602. Bad cwd: -32003. All 99 bibs in use: -32602. cols and rows of 0 mean the defaults 80 and 24.

name.description: Trimmed of leading and trailing Unicode whitespace, then 1-64 Unicode scalar values (Go runes, not bytes or grapheme clusters), with no control characters (Unicode Cc), else -32602. Omitted, or empty after trimming, means the agent's display name.

SessionKillParams.description: session.kill -> {}. An id matching neither the managed nor the unmanaged id pattern: -32602 with data.reason. Unknown managed id: -32001. Any `u_` id: -32007 not_managed, decided from the id alone; the user's tmux socket is never touched.

SessionRenameParams.description: session.rename -> Session. name: Trimmed of leading and trailing Unicode whitespace, then 1-64 Unicode scalar values (Go runes, not bytes or grapheme clusters), with no control characters (Unicode Cc); empty after trimming is -32602. An id matching neither id pattern: -32602 with data.reason. Unknown managed id: -32001. Any `u_` id: -32007.

SessionCaptureParams.description: session.capture -> SessionCaptureResult. Read-only; works for managed and unmanaged sessions. lines: history lines above the visible screen, 1-10000, default 1000; the visible rows are always included after them. With join true a wrapped line counts as several rows, so the result can hold fewer lines than `lines`. join: rejoin lines the terminal wrapped, default true. lines outside 1-10000, or an id matching neither id pattern: -32602. Unknown id: -32001.

SessionCaptureResult.description: text: plain text with no escape sequences and no trailing blank rows. When the JSON-encoded reply would not fit in one frame (1 MiB; escaping makes characters such as <, >, &, quotes and newlines take 2 to 6 bytes), the oldest lines are dropped, the newest are kept whole, and truncated is true. Text over 900000 bytes is cut the same way.

SessionAttachCommandParams.description: session.attachCommand. Works for managed and unmanaged sessions. An id matching neither id pattern: -32602 with data.reason. Unknown id: -32001.

SessionAttachCommandResult.description: argv to run on the host: [tmux path, "-u", socket args..., "attach-session", "-t", "=" + tmux session name]. The tmux path is absolute whenever the helper found tmux, so it runs under the minimal PATH of an SSH exec channel. Managed: [tmux, "-u", "-L", label, "attach-session", "-t", "=s_..."]. Unmanaged: [tmux, "-u", "attach-session", "-t", "=" + name]. A name ending in ";" has a backslash inserted before that ";", because tmux reads a trailing ";" as a command separator. An SSH exec request carries one command string that the host account's login shell parses, so clients executing argv over an SSH exec channel must POSIX single-quote every element, argv[0] included, and join the quoted elements with single spaces. The quoting rule: wrap the element in ' and replace each ' inside it with the four characters '\'' (close the quote, a backslash-escaped quote, reopen). For example it's becomes 'it'\''s'. The rule assumes a POSIX shell (sh, bash, zsh, dash, ksh).

installed.description: Command found on the user's login-shell PATH. Always true for shell.

AgentsListResult.description: agents.list. Order in v1: claude (Claude Code), omp (OMP), codex (Codex), opencode (OpenCode), shell (Shell).

FsRecentDirsResult.description: fs.recentDirs. Absolute paths of folders used for session.create, newest first, deduplicated. When none are recorded: [home directory].

FsListDirParams.description: fs.listDir. path must be absolute or start with ~ (expanded to the home directory); relative paths, NUL bytes, missing paths, non-directories and directories the user cannot read are -32003. showHidden (default false) includes names starting with a dot. includeFiles (default false) lists files and symlinks as well as directories; symlinks are never followed. With ref (git.v1), id is required and path is relative to the session cwd: the listing is the tree at that commit, with the same -32003 rules as fs.read. root (gitwrite.v1) needs id and makes path relative to the root of the repository holding the session cwd, as in fs.read; without ref it lists that folder on disk.

FsListDirResult.description: path is the cleaned absolute path that was listed. Without includeFiles, entries are subdirectories only (symlinks to directories included, at a ref only trees), with dir true and no kind or size. With includeFiles, entries are directories, regular files and symlinks, each with kind; dir is true only for kind dir; size (bytes) is given for files only; symlinks are reported as kind symlink and not followed; submodules, sockets, devices and pipes are left out. Sorted case-insensitively by name, at most 2000.

RequestId.description: Approval id: `r_` + 10 chars of lowercase unpadded base32.

HostId.description: Host id: `h_` + the first 26 chars of lowercase unpadded base32 of SHA-256(mailbox secret).

JobId.description: Job id: `j_` + 10 chars of lowercase unpadded base32.

Key32.description: A 32-byte key in base64url without padding (43 chars).

SessionMeta.description: What agent hooks and status-line payloads report about a session. Each field is null until reported.

ApprovalOption.description: One answer offered by the prompt. n is the number the agent's menu shows; option:<n> picks it.

Subject.description: The one thing an approval asks about, so notifications, the Live Activity and the Watch can show it without screen text. text counts Unicode scalar values and allows no control characters (Unicode Cc) other than newline and no bidirectional or zero-width characters (U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069, U+200B-200F, U+061C, U+2060, U+FEFF).

Approval.description: A question waiting for the user. Only pending approvals are listed or sent; the end of one is the approval.closed event.

source.description: hook: an agent permission hook; screen: the prompt-shape detector; ask: `togo ask`.

subject.description: Absent or null when the helper found no subject; detail then still describes the request. When set, detail is subject.text truncated to 256 characters, for apps that do not read subject.

snippet.description: Last lines of the pane around the prompt, at most 40 lines and 4096 bytes.

Decision.description: approve | deny | option:<n> (1-99, no leading zero) | text:<1-2000 Unicode scalar values (not UTF-16 units), no control characters (Unicode Cc)>. approve picks the first option with role approve (never approve_always); deny picks the first with role deny, else sends Escape. option:<n> naming no offered option and text: when allowText is false are -32602. Answers arriving through the relay mailbox may only be approve, deny or option:<n>.

Event.description: params of the `event` notification. The kind-specific fields sit beside the header fields. seq is strictly increasing per daemon and starts at 1. Every subscriber receives every event (no per-connection filtering), so a seq gap always means lost events and the client must call events.subscribe again. The helper writes the events.subscribe response before any event for that subscription; a client drops every event with seq <= the response seq. sessionId equals session.id for kind session, is non-null for session.removed and approval.open/closed of a session, and is null for events that belong to no session (notify and job without a session).

SessionRefParams.description: Params naming one session: git.status, git.branches, ports.list. Bad id: -32602; unknown: -32001.

EventsSubscribeParams.description: events.subscribe. Starts event notifications on this connection and returns a snapshot. foreground (default true) says the app is on screen, which suppresses pushes for sessions the app shows; call again to change it. Foreground is a lease: it lapses 45 s after the last request the connection sent, and any request renews it. An idle app on screen calls events.keepalive about every 20 s.

EventsKeepaliveParams.description: events.keepalive. Does nothing but, like every request, renews the connection's foreground lease (see EventsSubscribeParams). Result is {}.

EventsSubscribeResult.description: events.subscribe result. seq is the seq of the last event already reflected in sessions and approvals (0 when none). This response is written before any event for the subscription; events with seq <= this seq are already in the snapshot and the client drops them. Calling events.subscribe again on the same connection returns a fresh snapshot under the same rule and does not duplicate the stream.

ApprovalListParams.description: approval.list. Pending approvals, oldest first, optionally for one session.

ApprovalAnswerParams.description: approval.answer. Unknown requestId: -32001. Malformed decision (see Decision) or option n not offered: -32602. Already answered, prompt gone or expired: -32006, and no keys reach the pane.

SessionSetMuteParams.description: session.setMute -> Session. Bad id or muted missing: -32602; unknown: -32001; u_ id: -32007.

PushPairParams.description: push.pair. x25519: the device's push-sealing public key; approvalKey: its Ed25519 answer-signing public key. Pairing an existing deviceId replaces it. Any field out of shape: -32602. platform is ios when absent. liveActivityStartToken is the push-to-start token for the Live Activity; liveActivityCommand (default false) lets Live Activity pushes carry command text.

PushPairResult.description: hostKey is the helper's X25519 public key, which seals answers sent through the relay mailbox.

GitStatusResult.description: git.status. A cwd outside any repository is repo false, root and branch null, zero counts and no files. branch is null on a detached HEAD. The helper runs git with repository config that executes programs disabled. A helper with gitwrite.v1 lists every untracked file on its own (never a folder entry, as git status --untracked-files=all), lists at most 2,000 files in git's order, and always sends truncated, true when it left files out. Absent truncated (an older helper) means false. A client must not offer an action on all changes (such as discarding everything) while truncated is true.

items.description: index and worktree are the porcelain v2 status letters, `.` when unchanged. fingerprint (gitwrite.v1) identifies the working-tree content; every untracked or changed file present in the working tree has one, and it is absent only when the path has no file there (deleted).

GitDiffParams.description: git.diff. path is relative to the repository root, like git.status paths, and the diff runs at the root, so a session in a subfolder of the repository diffs any path git.status lists. ref diffs the working tree (or the index with staged) against that commit. commit (gitwrite.v1) diffs that commit against its first parent, a root commit against the empty tree; commit with staged true or with ref is -32602. Path, ref or commit rules as fs.read: -32003.

GitDiffResult.description: diff is unified text capped at 512 KiB; binary lists paths whose content differs but is not shown.

GitLogParams.description: git.log. ref defaults to HEAD, limit to 50. A ref starting with - or not resolving: -32003.

GitBranchesResult.description: git.branches. Local branches by name. Outside a repository: current null, no branches.

GitPathsParams.description: git.stage, git.unstage, git.discard (gitwrite.v1). Paths are relative to the repository root, like git.status paths. Each path names one file (GitWritePath) and follows the fs.read rules (-32003); a path of more than 4,096 bytes, with a NUL, ending in / or naming a directory is -32602, so a write never acts on a whole folder. The helper reads a fresh status first and refuses the whole call with -32006 stale when a path is not in it with a change the method acts on (stage: worktree change, untracked or unmerged; unstage: index change; discard: any change), or when seen has the path and either its status differs from the fresh letters or its fingerprint differs from a freshly computed one (one present and the other absent also differs). A file edited again keeps its letters but changes its fingerprint. Paths with a filter attribute (such as Git LFS) are -32006 filtered, a held index.lock is -32006 locked, and git.discard of an unmerged path is -32006 unmerged; in each case nothing is changed. git.discard acts on each path by itself: a path in HEAD has its index entry and working-tree file restored to HEAD (staged and unstaged changes both go); a path not in HEAD (untracked, or added in the index only) is removed from the index if there and its file is deleted. A path staged as a rename (index R) undoes the rename: its origPath is restored to HEAD in the index and working tree in the same write, and the new path is removed; the call is -32006 stale when anything is on disk at origPath under any letter case (a listed, ignored or untracked file, a link or a folder), or when seen has the new path but not origPath with the same status and no fingerprint, and -32006 case_rename when origPath differs from the path only in letter case. The partial changed list includes origPath when it changed. Nothing else changes: no other path, no ignored file and no folder. git.unstage of a path staged as a rename also puts its origPath back in the index. The result is the status after the write. Paths are passed to git literally, after --, and no hook, filter or other repository-configured program runs.

seen.description: Optional for git.stage and git.unstage; git.discard needs an entry for every path (-32602 otherwise). For each path, what git.status reported when the user chose it: status is the index and worktree letters, index first (".M" is a worktree change, "??" an untracked file), and fingerprint is the entry's fingerprint, absent when the entry had none. For a staged rename the client also sends its origPath with the rename's status and no fingerprint, so git.discard restores only the old path the user saw.

GitWritePath.description: One file path for a git write: 1 to 4,096 UTF-8 bytes (the schema can only bound characters) with no NUL. A path ending in / is also -32602; that rule is pinned by a fixture rather than this schema.

GitFingerprint.description: Content id of a working-tree file, compared only for equality. blob:<hash> is git's blob hash of the file bytes as stored without filters (git hash-object --no-filters), used for regular files up to 8,388,608 bytes while the blob-hashed files so far in the status list (git's order) total at most 268,435,456 bytes. stat:<size>:<mtime_ns> is the lstat size in bytes and modification time in nanoseconds since the epoch, used for larger files, for symlinks, and for every regular file from the first one that would pass that total.

GitCommitParams.description: git.commit (gitwrite.v1). Commits the index with message, or replaces the HEAD commit with amend. message is 1 to 65,536 UTF-8 bytes, its first line is not empty after trimming, and it has no control characters other than \n and \t; otherwise -32602. amend without head is -32602. Nothing staged without amend is -32006 nothing_staged, amend with no commit yet is -32006 unborn_amend, a missing git user.name or user.email is -32006 identity, a held index.lock is -32006 locked, and head that is no longer HEAD is -32006 stale. Hooks and commit signing never run.

head.description: The HEAD commit hash the user saw: required with amend (the commit it replaces), optional otherwise.

GitConflictData.description: -32006 data for a git write. stale: a path or HEAD no longer matches what the client saw. locked: another git process holds the index lock. filtered: a path has a filter attribute. unmerged: a conflicted path that the method does not act on. nothing_staged, identity, unborn_amend: see GitCommitParams. case_rename: git.discard of a rename that only changes letter case, which the helper does not undo. For all of these nothing changed. partial: the write failed after changing some paths; changed lists the paths whose status differs from before the call, and the client should refresh. raced: git.commit made commit hash, but another process moved HEAD between the helper's check and the commit, so its parent is not the HEAD the user saw; nothing is rewritten.

FsReadParams.description: fs.read. path is relative to the session cwd; absolute paths, .. escapes, symlinks resolving outside the cwd, missing files and non-files are -32003. ref reads the file at that commit (a ref starting with - is -32003). root (gitwrite.v1) makes path relative to the root of the repository holding the session cwd instead, the form git.status paths take; the same -32003 rules apply against the root, and a session outside a repository is -32003.

FsReadResult.description: path echoes the cleaned relative path. size is the full file size in bytes; content holds at most 512 KiB, base64url without padding (the protocol-wide rule) when the bytes are not valid UTF-8.

FsUploadParams.description: fs.upload (upload.v1). Writes the bytes for the agent to read, such as a screenshot. sessionId must be a managed session id (an unmanaged one is -32007, an unknown one -32001; any other string is -32602). name is reduced to the characters A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - and at most 64 bytes, keeping the extension; directory parts and leading dots are dropped. data is base64url without padding; more than 700000 decoded bytes is -32602.

FsUploadResult.description: path is the absolute path on the host of the file written, mode 0600 under $TOGO_HOME/uploads/<sessionId>/ as <unix-ms>-<name>. The helper deletes uploads older than 7 days.

PortsListResult.description: ports.list. TCP ports in the LISTEN state held by processes in the session's process tree, ordered by port.

LocalSignalParams.description: local.signal -> {}. Sent by `togo tap` for a bell, an OSC 9 or OSC 777 notification, or the first output after quiet. local.* methods are served only by the daemon, on connections it accepts on its unix socket from the same user; `serve --stdio` proxies to that socket, so its connections get them too. The in-process server that `serve --stdio` falls back to without a daemon does not serve them.

LocalHookParams.description: local.hook -> {}. One agent hook invocation, reduced by the adapter; the raw payload is never forwarded.

LocalAskParams.description: local.ask. Opens an approval with source ask and blocks until it is answered or timeoutSec passes.

approve.description: The option a notification's Approve picks, matched case-insensitively. Absent: inferred from the labels (Approve, Yes, Allow, Accept, Continue).

deny.description: The option a notification's Deny picks, matched case-insensitively. Absent: inferred from the labels (Deny, No, Reject, Cancel, Stop).

LocalNotifyParams.description: local.notify. strict makes `togo notify` exit non-zero when nothing was delivered.

LocalNotifyResult.description: delivered is true when a subscriber or a paired device received it.

LocalJobParams.description: local.job. start needs name and returns a new jobId; update and end need jobId; end takes status (default ok).

PushPlaintext.description: Plaintext sealed (label push, aad hostId + "|" + deviceId) into the ciphertext of a relay push, encoded as compact UTF-8 JSON. kind needs_you announces an approval: requestId and options are required. kind clear withdraws the notification for requestId (required; the approval closed): title and body are empty strings and options is absent. done, job and notify carry no requestId or options. sessionId, bib and agent are null when the event belongs to no session. ts is Unix time in milliseconds when the helper sealed it. The push is not signed by the host; a forged push can only change what the phone displays, since answers are bound to the host's requestIds. subject (needs_you only, absent when unknown) is the approval's structured subject; host is the machine's display name (`hostname -s`, at most 64 characters). Both are optional so older payloads stay valid.

AnswerPlaintext.description:
Plaintext sealed (label answer, aad hostId) by the phone and posted to the relay mailbox, encoded as compact UTF-8 JSON. decision is limited to approve, deny and option:<n>; text answers travel only over SSH. ts is Unix time in milliseconds on the phone. sig is the Ed25519 signature, base64url without padding (86 chars), by the device's approvalKey over the UTF-8 bytes of "togo-approval/v1
" + hostId + "
" + requestId + "
" + decision + "
" + ts, where ts is written in decimal ASCII without leading zeros, each field is exactly the value in this object (hostId from push.pair), and there is no trailing newline. Senders omit type on answers, because helpers that predate it reject unknown fields; receivers accept it absent or "answer". Only RegisterPlaintext, which shares the mailbox, carries a type.

RegisterPlaintext.description:
Plaintext sealed (label answer, aad hostId) by a paired device and posted to the relay mailbox when its tokens or its command text choice change, encoded as compact UTF-8 JSON. A token left out keeps the stored one. liveActivityCommand replaces the stored choice (see PairParams). ts is Unix time in milliseconds on the device. sig is the Ed25519 signature, base64url without padding (86 chars), by the device's approvalKey over the UTF-8 bytes of "togo-register/v2
" + hostId + "
" + deviceId + "
" + apnsToken + "
" + liveActivityToken + "
" + liveActivityStartToken + "
" + liveActivityCommand + "
" + ts, where an absent token is the empty string, liveActivityCommand is "true" or "false", ts is decimal ASCII without leading zeros, and there is no trailing newline.

LiveContentState.description: Live Activity content state, sent by the helper to the relay in the clear and shown by the app. since is Unix time in seconds when the status began. requestId is the approval the Approve button answers, null unless status is needs_you. command is null unless the device opted in with liveActivityCommand.

LiveAttributes.description: Live Activity attributes sent with a push-to-start.

PlaintextFixture.description: A sealed-payload example in protocol/v1/fixtures/plaintext. Shape only: protocol/fixtures/crypto holds the seal and signature vectors.

Fixture.description: Golden exchange in protocol/v1/fixtures. A harness starts a fresh connection, sends each `setup` request in order (each reply must be a success response; its result is not compared), then sends `request` and compares the reply to `response` semantically: same keys and values, with two placeholder rules for strings in `response`. (1) The string "<any>" matches any value (the key must still be present); it is used only for genuinely host-dependent values (tmux path and socket label in argv, os, arch, the -32602 reason text, git.commit hashes, which depend on the host clock; so the git.commit result is checked for shape only, not against GitCommitResult). (2) A string starting with "<home>" is replaced by the harness HOME path followed by the rest of the string ("<home>/proj" means HOME + "/proj"; "<home>" alone means HOME) and then compared exactly. Harness environment shared by all fixtures: a fresh, empty tmux server on a test label; no unmanaged sessions (user socket disabled); session ids come from a seam returning "s_abcdefghij"; the clock reads 2026-11-03T12:00:00Z; helper version "0.0.0-test", hostname "testhost"; HOME (and the API's home) is a fresh temp dir, given as an absolute path with symlinks resolved (so tmux's pane path equals it), holding directories `alpha`, `Beta`, `proj`, `.cache` and a regular file `notes.txt` (byte order Beta, alpha, proj differs from the case-insensitive order alpha, Beta, proj); TOGO_HOME is a separate fresh temp dir; the login-shell PATH contains none of claude, omp, codex, opencode. Per-fixture deviations are stated in `description`.
